title: FULL OUTER JOIN for Data Reconciliation
realWorldScenario: Finance and inventory auditing teams need to reconcile orders and payments to identify orders without payments and orphan payments without orders.
questionStatement: Write a query using a `FULL OUTER JOIN` between `orders` and `payments` on `orders.id = payments.order_id`. Return `orders.id` as `order_id`, `payments.id` as `payment_id`, `orders.total_amount`, and `payments.amount` as `payment_amount`, ordered by `order_id` ascending, `payment_id` ascending.
starterCode:
-- Reconcile orders and payments with FULL OUTER JOIN
SELECT
  o.id AS order_id,
  p.id AS payment_id,
  o.total_amount,
  p.amount AS payment_amount
FROM orders o
FULL OUTER JOIN payments p ON o.id = p.order_id
ORDER BY o.id ASC, p.id ASC;
hints: FULL OUTER JOIN keeps rows from both tables even when there is no match.

testCases.description: Verify bilateral reconciliation of orders and payment attempts
